turns.prompt_text: I have an old nintendo ds game with a pokemon on it, can I rewrite it?
turns.response_html:
It is a common question, and the short answer is: No, you cannot "rewrite" or replace the actual game on an official Nintendo DS cartridge.

The technology used in those cartridges is ROM (Read-Only Memory). The game data is "burned" onto the chip at the factory during manufacturing. Unlike a USB drive or an SD card, the hardware itself is physically incapable of being overwritten with a different game (e.g., you can't turn a copy of Pokémon Diamond into Pokémon Platinum).

However, depending on what you actually want to achieve, there are a few "hacker" workarounds that people in the community use.

1. You CAN rewrite the "Save File"

If your goal isn't to change the game itself, but rather to change your team, give yourself items, or back up your progress to a computer, you can do that.

  • On a 3DS: If you have a modded 3DS, you can use a tool called Checkpoint or GodMode9 to extract your Pokémon save file, edit it on a PC (using a program like PKHeX), and then "inject" it back into the cartridge.
  • On a DS Lite: You can use a "Flashcart" (like an R4 card) and homebrew software to back up or restore saves to an official cartridge in the slot.

2. If you want to play different games (Flashcarts)

Since official cartridges can't be rewritten, most people who want to play various games (or fan-made "ROM hacks") on original hardware use a Flashcart (commonly known as an R4 card).

  • These look like a standard DS game but have a slot for a MicroSD card.
  • You can put as many games as you want on that SD card and "rewrite" it as often as you like.

3. "Reproduction" Cartridges

If you see Pokémon games for very cheap on sites like eBay or AliExpress, those are usually "repro" carts. Unlike official Nintendo carts, these are often made with Flash memory rather than ROM.

  • Technically, with very specialized hardware (like a GBxcart RW or a Joey Jr.), some of these bootleg cartridges can be rewritten, but it is hit-or-miss and often results in the cartridge breaking.

A Note on Perspectives: From a collector’s perspective, official Pokémon cartridges are currently very valuable (often $100+ USD). From a preservationist's perspective, the fact that they are Read-Only is actually a good thing—it ensures the original data stays intact for decades without being accidentally corrupted or erased.
